latin_text: He had already adorned the supercelestial region with intelligences, enlivened the heavenly globes with eternal souls, and filled the excremental and filthy parts of the lower world with a multitude of forms of animal life.
english_translation: He had already adorned the supercelestial region with intelligences, enlivened the heavenly globes with eternal souls, and filled the excremental and filthy parts of the lower world with a multitude of forms of animal life.
exegesis:
Pico paints the cosmological canvas before human creation: God completes the hierarchical universe in three tiers—supercelestial (angelical intelligences), celestial (ensouled spheres), sublunary (material creation). [VERIFIED] This three-world cosmology draws on Pseudo-Dionysius (hierarchy of intelligences beyond the cosmos), Aquinas (celestial spheres as loci of angelic governance), and the Neoplatonic emanationist model. Each tier is fully populated with appropriate beings: angels perform their eternal contemplation, heavenly bodies execute their eternal motions, sublunary matter churns in generation and corruption. The passage establishes a complete cosmos of determinate essences, each fulfilling its appointed nature—until humanity enters the scene.

The philosophical function of this passage is crucial: it describes a universe in equilibrium, where every being has found its place. Pico emphasizes that this creation is already perfect, complete, and lacking nothing. Angels, though pure intellects, are bound to their hierarchical roles. The celestial bodies, though eternal, are bound to their spheres. Material creation, though chaotic, is bound by divine order. This completeness throws into sharp relief the enigma of human creation: into a finished cosmos, what new thing can God create? What role remains? Pico's answer—that humans are created precisely to transcend and transform within this hierarchy—depends on understanding that the pre-human universe, though perfect in its kind, is fundamentally static and determined.

[INFERRED] In Heptaplus 3.3 and the broader cosmological framework, this three-world hierarchy becomes the scaffolding for Pico's seven-layer interpretive method. Each text—oration, heptaplus, commento, being and unity—elaborates the metaphysical density of this simple tripartite structure. The Commento's treatment of the three hypostases (intelligible world, celestial soul, material being) parallels this cosmological trinity. Being & Unity grounds it metaphysically in participated being: angels participate in divine being most directly, celestial bodies through motion, material things through static form.
notes: Describing the first cosmological moment: God creates a hierarchical cosmos with angels (intelligences) in the supercelestial realm. Humans have not yet been created.
